profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential - Denver - Centennial Data Center) is located at 12500 East Arapahoe Road, Ste C, Centennial, CO 80112. The operator publishes a footprint of 43294 square feet and 1.6 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, ITAR, NIST 800-53, HITRUST, SSAE 18. This building sits in the Denver-Aurora corridor local reporting has dubbed "Data Center Row," which also includes a major QTS facility under construction in Aurora. Xcel Energy, the region's dominant utility, said in 2025 it was seeking to invest $22 billion to add 12 to 14 gigawatts of new generation and transmission capacity by 2040, driven substantially by data center demand; the utility reported pending data center applications for 5.8 gigawatts of electricity, nearly matching its entire existing 6.2-gigawatt Colorado generating capacity, with data center load projected to reach 8.5 gigawatts by 2040, per Colorado Sun's reporting. The Colorado Public Utilities Commission has voiced skepticism about the reliability of these forecasts, noting that between October and May alone, seven data center prospects representing 4 gigawatts withdrew requests while more than a dozen new prospects totaling 3.5 gigawatts filed applications, with regulators and consumer advocates warning that ratepayers could face stranded-asset costs if projected demand fails to materialize.

The QTS facility anchoring the Aurora side of "Data Center Row" is planned at 177 megawatts of capacity on 80 acres at the I-70/C-470 interchange, positioned to become Xcel Energy's largest industrial customer in Colorado, on par with Evraz Rocky Mountain Steel in Pueblo, a marked shift from Xcel's historical major customers in mining and manufacturing, per Colorado Sun's 2023 reporting. That single campus is expected to require 160 megawatts of peak load delivered via a $28 million high-voltage transmission line, ramping up over roughly a decade, with Xcel anticipating similar-scale loads from other emerging data center customers in the region. For QTS, electricity was reported to represent about 40% of operating costs, underscoring why competitive utility rates were central to the Aurora site decision, a dynamic shared broadly across Colorado's Front Range data center corridor.

profile.regional_context: Denver-Aurora has become known locally as "Data Center Row," a corridor drawing major new investment including a QTS facility under construction in Aurora, alongside Xcel Energy's multi-billion-dollar generation and transmission expansion plans and regulatory debate over who bears the cost risk if projected data center demand does not fully materialize.

reading.body:
The Flexential Centennial data center operates 1.6 MW of IT capacity, roughly 40 racks at AI training density or 100 to 160 high-end accelerators, though the operator does not publish its workload mix.

The facility's published certifications address security, compliance, and defense contractor requirements. They indicate readiness for regulated workloads, not the sustained high-utilization profiles typical of large-scale AI training or inference. This pattern matters because certified facilities can command pricing premium to commodity capacity, but compliance focus often correlates with lower power density and higher cost per compute unit than purpose-built AI infrastructure.

Flexential operates this site as part of a 40-plus facility portfolio across 18 national markets, but publishes capacity data for only this one location. The operator's regional footprint spans the Western United States, inherited from the ViaWest and Peak 10 merger completed in 2018. Without disclosed capacity figures at other Flexential sites, the distribution of compute across their portfolio and the concentration of AI workloads within it remain invisible. This opacity is common among regional data center operators and limits tracking of actual infrastructure expansion against AI demand.
